15152139_c025cc8f.text: The populations of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-expressing hypothalamic cells are sexually dimorphic in rats and mice (Simerly, 1989) (Simerly et al., 1985). TH-immunoreactive (ir) positive neurons in the anteroventral periventricular nucleus (AVPv) of the preoptic region regulating gonadotropin release are necessary for female ovulation, whose numbers in a female, in addition to their size difference, are two to four times greater than in a male (Simerly et al., 1985)(Simerly, 1989)(Simerly et al., 1985)(Wiegand et al., 1982). Ovariectomy of the female does not affect TH expression, while chronic treatment with high levels of estradiol reduces its expression (Simerly et al., 1985)(Simerly, 1989).
